correctness.rationale: The explicit formula Delta=H(p+q+1)-pq is exact. Positivity bounds p by H+floor(sqrt(H(H+1))). The divisor condition bounds q by H(p+1) in both p<H and p>H cases; p=H is ruled out by valuation. The standalone prime enumeration checks all remaining 51 filtered prime pairs, discovers exactly five solutions and independently recomputes their divisor sums. Exhaustiveness follows from mathematical bounds; computations are actual, finite, exact and replayable.

originality.rationale: The five numbers are not new: they appear in the 2013 Ren–Chen example list and OEIS. The assessed claim instead proves that these are the only n=2^a p q with a=1,2,3. Ren–Chen Theorem 1.2 classifies TWO prime supports, not three, and labels finiteness for a fixed 3+ prime support as a conjecture. The original Shevelev constructions also have two prime supports. Mathematically related archived results deal with a=1 constraints or different divisor identities and cannot imply the complete a=3 spectrum.

value.rationale: The motivating problem is Ren–Chen Conjecture 1.3 on fixed prime support. The one-omission equation is subtle even in the three-prime squarefree-odd-part family. The first two dyadic layers vanish while the third is the first populated layer, and the statement proves a natural COMPLETE first nonempty classification with unbounded p,q, not just new entries in a table. The derived effective finite-prime bound is an exact structural sieve. It does not claim a result for all a or settle the general conjecture.
